title: Cascade corpus scenario file
description: One family of cascade confirmation scenarios (tap_grid/cascade_corpus, Issue# 578 - tap). Each scenario is a small graph built from grid_fixtures' playground vocabulary, one delete operation, and the hand-authored outcome it must produce. The reference model in model_oracle.py must agree with every expected block at load time.

family.description: The family this file covers: depth, loops, blocks, limits or records. One family per file.

description.description: What this family exercises and why it matters, for a reader who opens only this file.

scenarios.description: The scenarios, in the order a reader should meet them (simplest first).

ref.description: A scenario-local name for a node or edge. Refs never leave the scenario; the runner maps them to minted entity ids.

name.description: Human-readable scenario name; unique within the corpus (it is the pytest id).

covers.description: The spec requirement and acceptance-criterion ids this scenario exercises. Binding: it feeds the traceability matrix.

pending.description: A known defect this scenario is waiting on, as `owner/repo#n`. While set, the scenario MUST fail (strict xfail); when the fix lands the scenario passes, the strict xfail fails, and the tag is removed. The corpus tracks known defects instead of papering over them.

containment.description: Per node type, the edge types that mean containment for the cascade (CONTAINMENT_EDGES, set on the model class for this scenario). A type absent here contains nothing: its outgoing edges are references.

blocked_types.description: Node types the public delete path may not touch for this scenario (INTERNAL_ONLY set on the model class). A cascade that reaches a node of such a type is refused whole; a plain delete of one is refused.

nodes.description: The nodes, by ref. Order is creation order; it carries no meaning for the outcome.

edges.description: The edges, by ref, from node ref to node ref. Creation order is the order the walk sees siblings; the loader rejects a scenario whose outcome would depend on that order.

type.description: A grid_fixtures playground edge type (PG_LINKS__grid_fixtures, PG_NESTS__grid_fixtures, PG_LOOPS__grid_fixtures, PG_OPTIONAL__grid_fixtures).

pre_retired.description: Node refs tombstoned (plain delete_node, reason `resolved`) BEFORE the operation runs, with their incident edges, or edge refs ended before it (delete_edge_by_entity) — for rerun, already-retired and retired-bridge scenarios. Their events are not part of the expected records.

verb.description: The only verb the corpus exercises today.

cascade.description: The cascade mode passed verbatim: `none` (default), `contained`, or a deliberately invalid value to prove the refusal.

reason.description: The reason passed verbatim; null means omitted (records `unspecified`). A value outside the closed vocabulary proves the refusal.

metadata.description: Metadata passed with the delete; inherited by every cascaded node and edge event.

cap.description: TAP_CASCADE_MAX_CLOSURE for this run (default 5000): the most nodes one contained cascade may discover, root included.

outcome.description: success: the operation returned success and exactly the listed nodes and edges are tombstoned. refused: the operation returned failure with error_code, nothing changed, no batch row survives, no event was written.

error_code.description: On refusal, the ServiceError code of the first error (cascade_closure_too_large, unsupported_operation, invalid_reason, validation_error, ...).

retired_nodes.description: Exactly the node refs that must be tombstoned by this operation (pre_retired ones excluded). Every other node must be untouched: still live, same version.

retired_edges.description: Exactly the edge refs that must be tombstoned by this operation. Every other edge must be untouched.

events.description: Hand-authored spot checks on the records, by node or edge ref: the reason the event carries and, for a cascaded one, the ref of the node it was a consequence of. The oracle checks the full event set; these are the human-readable subset a reader can verify by eye.

count.description: How many delete/unlink events this ref must carry after the operation (default 1 for a retired ref).

note.description: Why this outcome is the right one, in one or two sentences a reader can check against the spec.
